title: America Has Also Run Out of EB-5 Investor Green Cards for Indians. The Queue Will Not Move Until October.
excerpt: A week after EB-2 visas hit their annual cap, the investor pathway has followed suit — leaving wealthy Indian applicants with no route to permanent residency until the new fiscal year begins.
body:
The United States has officially exhausted its annual allocation of EB-5 investor visas for Indian nationals, the Department of State confirmed this week. No new EB-5 unreserved visas will be issued to Indian applicants until the next fiscal year opens on October 1, 2026.

The freeze follows the same pattern that hit EB-2 professionals just days earlier. Together, the two closures mean that both of the primary employment-based green card pathways available to Indians — one for skilled workers with advanced degrees, the other for investors willing to commit at least $800,000 to American businesses — are now shut for the remainder of the fiscal year.

## What Happened

According to the Department of State's June 2026 Visa Bulletin, all available EB-5 "unreserved" category visas for India were used up as of June 5. The EB-5 programme allows foreign nationals to obtain permanent residency by making qualifying investments in U.S. businesses that create or preserve at least 10 jobs.

The exhaustion was driven by a familiar structural bottleneck: the per-country cap. Under the Immigration and Nationality Act, no single country can receive more than 7 per cent of the total employment-based and family-sponsored immigrant visas in any fiscal year. For a country like India, where demand from affluent applicants consistently outstrips supply, the ceiling becomes a hard wall.

Even the addition of unused reserved visas from fiscal year 2024 — rolled over under the EB-5 Reform and Integrity Act of 2022 — was not enough to meet demand.

## What It Means for NRI Investors

The impact falls hardest on Indian entrepreneurs and high-net-worth families who have been waiting — in some cases for years — for their EB-5 petitions to be processed. Many have already made their qualifying investments, created the required jobs, and completed every step of the application. The only thing left was the visa number itself. That number is now unavailable.

For those in the middle of relocation plans, the pause means months of limbo. Business timelines, children's school enrolments, and real estate transactions that were calibrated around a 2026 arrival will need to be renegotiated.

There is a partial silver lining. The Visa Bulletin indicates that EB-5 set-aside categories — including Rural, High Unemployment Area, and Infrastructure projects — remain current for Indian applicants. Investors who strategically chose projects in these categories may still be able to proceed, though processing times remain unpredictable.

## The Bigger Picture

The back-to-back closures of EB-2 and EB-5 categories expose the structural strain that the per-country cap places on Indian nationals across every tier of the immigration system. Whether you are a software engineer with a master's degree or a business owner willing to invest nearly a million dollars, the bottleneck is the same: a fixed annual quota that does not scale with demand.

Immigration attorneys have long argued that the 7 per cent per-country limit, designed in an era of far lower demand, is fundamentally incompatible with modern migration patterns. Multiple legislative proposals to eliminate or raise the cap have stalled in Congress over the past decade.

For now, the queue resets on October 1. Fresh visa numbers will become available, priority dates will advance, and the cycle will begin again. But the underlying arithmetic has not changed. Demand from India will likely exhaust the new allocation just as quickly — perhaps even faster, as a growing pool of approved petitions competes for the same finite number of slots.

The EB-5 Reform and Integrity Act of 2022 introduced grandfathering protections for Regional Center petitions filed by September 30, 2026. Investors considering the programme would be wise to file before that deadline, even if the visa itself will not be available for months or years.

*Sources: U.S. Department of State June 2026 Visa Bulletin; USCIS EB-5 programme guidance; EB-5 Reform and Integrity Act of 2022*
nri_angle: Indian investors who have committed hundreds of thousands of dollars to U.S. businesses now face months of limbo, with no EB-5 visas available until October — the second employment-based pathway to close on them in a week.
author: Diaspora Desk
